author: reek
body: Compress, decompress, verify byte identity -- and verify the output is SMALLER on run-heavy input, the assertion a pass-through cannot pass.

author: reek
body: brotli-compress emitted only stored meta-blocks and inflated everything. RLE meta-blocks now give real compression on runs. A round-trip alone cannot tell a compressor from a pipe, so the size assertion runs on a compressible input: two long runs. The mixed input exercises the stored-block fallback and the RLE/stored boundary in one round-trip.

author: reek
body: Literals, then a run, then literals: exercises stored fallback and both block boundaries in a single round-trip.

author: reek
body: Prose, for block splitting. Words drawn from a small vocabulary by a carried linear congruential state -- carried rather than indexed, so the text does not become periodic and collapse into a single long match. That gives MANY short commands, which is what block splitting needs: an input the matcher turns into two or three long copies has nothing to cut.

author: reek
body: A hundred and ninety DISTINCT corpus words. What this input is for is not the dictionary but the CODE-LENGTH REPAIR underneath it: many distinct words give many distinct insert-and-copy symbols, and a description over about twenty of them is what used to defeat the repair.

author: reek
body: THE PIN IS ON THE SIZE, NOT ON THE ROUND-TRIP, and it has to be: the round-trip passed the whole time. A discarded plan is not a wrong answer, it is a silently worse one, so only a size can see it.

author: reek
body: Corpus words each followed by one of the dictionary's own phrase suffixes -- " of the ", " and ", ", " -- which is what the word transforms exist for. A transform is a word plus an affix, so an input where those affixes actually occur is the only place the search can pay.

author: reek
body: An order-one source with sixty-four genuinely distinct conditional distributions: each context draws from its own six-byte alphabet, so the contexts cluster into more than four groups and a fifth tree onwards has real work to do.
